title: potentilla supina subsp. paradoxa
intro: Potentilla supina subsp. paradoxa, commonly known as the "dwarf cinquefoil," is a plant species in the Rosaceae family, characterized by its small, five-petaled flowers and shrub-like growth habit. It has been traditionally used in medicine due to its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which can help to soothe digestive issues, reduce fever, and treat wounds. The therapeutic actions of Potentilla supina subsp. paradoxa include its ability to modulate the immune system, protect against oxidative stress, and exhibit antiviral and antibacterial activities. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and are responsible for its therapeutic actions.
